claim: Schemas bias recall toward the reader's current perspective: shifting perspective after reading raises recall of newly relevant ideas (+7.1% vs -2.9% control, N=39) and lowers old-perspective recall in the shift-only design (-21%, N=16).
agent_test: Give the agent a task-perspective prompt after reading a long document; measure recall of perspective-relevant vs irrelevant facts at equal tokens.

claim: Schema-congruent material is learned faster and more accurately, but not remembered better item by item: incongruent items had higher recognition d-prime (2.31 vs 1.88 global; N=48); congruency benefits are mostly for associative and gist memory. Meta-analysis (Rojahn and Pettigrew 1992, 60 studies, 165 tests) shows the direction depends on the measure: guessing-corrected recall and recognition favour inconsistent items, uncorrected recognition favours consistent items.
agent_test: Compare agent recall of schema-fitting vs schema-violating facts after summary compression; check whether violations are dropped or kept.

claim: Schema-driven memory distortion is reduced but not removed by direct rebuttal: prediction-based false memory fell from 0.153 to 0.035 (Exp 1a, N=71) yet stayed above zero, and survived a 24h delay.
agent_test: Insert a verify-against-source step before answering; count how often schema-consistent unsupported details survive.

claim: Schema typicality pulls reconstructions toward category centres; semantic category structure beats visual similarity as the pull; the effect vanishes when items are not arranged by category.
agent_test: Check agent summaries for regression to the typical member of a category (atypical numbers rounded to typical).

claim: Findings on schema clustering effects are fragile: Cockcroft et al (2022) found inconclusive or absent memory effects (d=0.35, BF01=0.87; none at 24h) across 4 experiments.
agent_test: Do not build on schema-clustering effects as a design basis without a within-agent test.

claim: Serial-reproduction chains converge on attractors in LLMs: attractor strength Continue > Take inspiration > Rephrase; toxicity the strongest attractor property; strength varies by model; GPT-4 chains move faster than human chains.
agent_test: Run repeated self-summarise loops on the agent notes for 10 and 50 rounds; track drift toward generic content at equal tokens.

claim: LLM summarising iterations keep stereotype-consistent, negative, social and threat content more than neutral content (beta 0.058 to 0.523), a human-like content bias.
agent_test: Measure what content survives the agent context compression; test whether threat, social or stereotype content is over-kept.

claim: Lossy memory can be worse than none: summaries that keep a conclusion but drop the derivation raise confident wrong emission (27% to 59% on an 8B model; 0% to 49% on Opus) and exact recovery after correction is 0.00.
agent_test: Keep source-first notes (derivation basis) vs summary-only notes; test exact recovery after a planted error and correction.

claim: Storing abstractions can hurt agents: error reproduction means anti-persistence memory beat trajectory and abstraction memory in all nine settings, and abstraction memory was below raw trajectory memory in seven of nine.
agent_test: Compare raw trajectory memory vs rule/skill memory over repeated tasks with a seeded wrong rule.

claim: Abstraction-style memory also helps in other agent studies (Agent Workflow Memory +24.6% Mind2Web, +51.1% WebArena; ExpeL ALFWorld 40.0 to 59.0; Reflexion 130/134), in tension with the error-reproduction result; the difference lies in error handling and benchmark.
agent_test: Run the same task stream with and without induced workflows, seeding some wrong workflows.

claim: Gist compression with look-up extends effective context 3.5x to 20x with equal or better accuracy than the full text (QuALITY 86.91 to 87.17% vs 85.83%): gist plus detail retrieval is a viable schema-like store.
agent_test: Compare full-context vs gist-plus-lookup at equal tokens on long inputs.

claim: LLMs rely on memorised priors over contrary evidence: GPT-4 memorisation ratio 80% on popular entities with mixed evidence; models accept coherent counter-evidence but cling to memory under substitution evidence; larger models more stubborn.
agent_test: Plant coherent vs substituted contrary evidence against a well-known fact; measure whether the agent updates.

claim: Counterfactual variants of familiar tasks lower LLM accuracy though it stays above chance, showing reliance on default task schemas.
agent_test: Run default vs counterfactual variants of a task; test whether an explicit list-the-assumed-defaults step closes the gap.

claim: Content effects (realistic rules help, abstract hurt) appear in LLMs as in humans on syllogisms and Wason; NLI is at ceiling.
agent_test: Test abstract vs realistic framing of one problem; check whether recasting into abstract form helps.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: LLMs fill gaps with stereotype schemas in pronoun resolution: 6.8x more likely to pick a stereotype-fitting female occupation, 3.4x for male, and give false explanations.
agent_test: Add a check that flags unsupported default role assumptions; measure accuracy on anti-stereotypical items.

claim: Distortion in verbal event recall is partly predictable by LLM features: false memory 27.4% of recalled events (N=229); semantic centrality raises recall odds 12%; corpus similarity predicts factual conflicts, surprisal predicts confabulations.
agent_test: Use LLM-estimated centrality to flag agent notes most at risk of distortion.

claim: Brewer and Treyens (1981) office-schema intrusion (false books) is widely cited, but its exact numbers were not read in this run. Gap search: still unverified; secondary pages give N=86 (35 s in office) in one place and 30 in others, so no N or rate may be cited.
agent_test: Retrieve the primary paper before using any figure.

claim: Bartlett War of the Ghosts results (series N=20; title omitted by 7; arrows excuse omitted by half) are small-sample and uncontrolled; later replications (Gauld and Stephenson 1967; Wynn and Logie 1998; Bergman and Roediger 1999) were not opened. Bergman and Roediger (1999) report a successful replication (tests at 15 min, 1 week, 6 months; distortion share rises with delay), abstract only.
agent_test: Treat as qualitative; do not cite rates.

claim: Schema theory lists five processes (attention direction, framework, instantiation, retrieval aid, output editing) but is largely qualitative and hard to falsify (Alba and Hasher critique, not opened).
agent_test: Do not implement schema as one generic module; test each process separately.

claim: Clone-structured graph and hierarchical active-inference models give formal schema learning (CSCG 95%+ next-token with enough clones, below 75% with 10), but are not testable by prompting alone.
agent_test: Not testable at present on prompting alone.

claim: Stale-state memory is a core agent failure: best model 55.2% on STALE, GPT-4o-mini plain 8.7% (LightMem 17.8%); models accept false premises about outdated state.
agent_test: Add timestamp and validity tags to notes; test update detection at equal tokens.

claim: Schema-congruency literature has a meta-analytic resolution (Rojahn and Pettigrew 1992): small overall advantage for schema-inconsistent items, direction set by test type (corrected vs uncorrected for guessing), delay, exposure and proportion of inconsistent items; no newer meta-analysis was found.
agent_test: Score agent note recall with a guessing correction; do not assume congruent items are always favoured.

claim: Bergman and Roediger (1999) replicated Bartlett's repeated-reproduction distortion with delays of 15 min, 1 week and 6 months: forgetting plus rationalisation, with the share of distorted material rising with delay. Only the abstract was read; no N or rates.
agent_test: Distortion grows with delay between rewrites; limit the number of rewrites per note.

claim: LLMs retain stereotype-consistent, negative, social and threat content over neutral content across transmission chains, and resolve ambiguity negatively (ChatGPT, five preregistered experiments, coefficients 0.058 to 0.523, all P<0.01).
agent_test: Log ambiguous source details unresolved; check summaries for negative or stereotype-fitting drift.

claim: Provenance availability is not provenance use: with a verification budget of two of six records, 16 models inspected the path behind a settled-sounding constraint in about 20% of episodes and followed the stale memory in 74.7% to 77.3% of superseded episodes; forcing one slot onto the critical path gained +61 to +81 points, and PlanFence derivation links fixed stale plans 30/30 vs 0/30.
agent_test: Store derivation links but also add an operator that forces opening the derivation of any stored limit or conclusion before acting after a correction. Test at equal tokens.

claim: Whole-context LLM rewriting can erase memory in one step: 18,282 tokens and 66.7 accuracy fell to 122 tokens and 57.1, below the 63.7 no-context baseline; incremental delta updates avoid this.
agent_test: Append small dated notes; never rewrite the whole memory in one call.

claim: Wrong entries in abstraction-style memory do limited damage when rare and large damage when constant: harmful bullets every step cost 4.0 points (66.7 vs 70.7 base), every 5 steps the playbook still gained 5.4; wrong raw records are also replayed (experience-following) and injected records are used (98.2% injection, 76.8% attack success). No arm compares a wrong rule to a wrong raw fact at equal tokens.
agent_test: Gap 2 still open: run a seeded wrong rule vs seeded wrong fact test at equal tokens before trusting abstraction memory.

claim: Counterfactual task variants lower accuracy even when a comprehension check shows the new rule is understood; chain-of-thought and 16-shot examples narrow but do not close the gap. No study tested an explicit step that lists assumed defaults.
agent_test: Test an assumptions-listing step against a plain chain-of-thought control at equal tokens.

claim: No LLM study was found that tests Bartlett's design directly (single-step recall of an unfamiliar story with rationalisation scoring) or LLM versions of the Brewer and Treyens office study; the closest are serial-reproduction studies of toxicity, positivity, length and stereotype retention and GPT-4 multimodal chains.
agent_test: Run our own small Bartlett probe on the agent if story recall matters.
